title: Structuring and smurfing
definition: The use of many small transactions, conducted by or for one person, so that the value is moved in amounts that fall below a reporting threshold, and the underlying activity is never reported as a single transaction. The defining feature is the relationship between the transaction and the reporting requirement it sits beneath, not the amount itself.
evidence_to_cite: the individual transactions, each cited by its own source id
the threshold in force and the aggregation rule applied
the evidence of common control between the accounts used
benign_explanations: A cash-intensive business whose takings genuinely fall below the threshold on ordinary days.
A customer who splits a payment across accounts for operational reasons such as daily limits.
A business depositing at several branches because each site banks its own takings.
A consumer who makes several small payments to different merchants on one occasion.

sources.citation: Financial Crimes Enforcement Network, guidance on the avoidance of reporting requirements, summarised in the FinCrime regulatory index.

notes: The typology is the *pattern*. Any single small transaction is ordinary, and the pattern is only visible across transactions, accounts and counterparties.
